sources.locator: "Battle of the Lake of Two Mountains", revision 1370600653

explanation: The article opens on the connection: "The battle occurred in response to the Lachine massacre of August 1689. In October, Governor General of New France, the Marquis de Denonville dispatched a scouting party of 28 coureur des bois … to search for Haudenosaunee warriors that posed a threat to residents on the Island of Montreal." The scouting party is what the massacre produced; the skirmish is what the party found. Wikipedia is the only author named, so probable.
